subject: Encord | Coffee, caps & an impossible triangle
text:
Bonjour [NAME], Martin,

Shame to have missed you at the office yesterday. I was in town for RAISE
so thought I'd drop by and drop a mystery package off.

Laurent kindly took the parcel in and has hopefully shared the photo:
coffee, caps for the Paris heat, and a 3D-printed Penrose triangle for the
maths nerds in the building (the [COMPANY] symbol being a triangle, after all).

Since you rightly do not train on customer data, everything rests on
curated gold-standard sets: that is exactly what Encord helps leading Audio
players like Kyutai and leading Healthcare teams like UnitedHealth Group
achieve.

I would love 15 mins to show you how this could look for [COMPANY]. If you say
the word, I can put some tentative time in the calendar for next week.

P.S. Martin - sorry you could not make the wine tasting our CEOs hosted on
Tuesday. [SENDER] (one of our CEOs) met [SENDER] LeBrun last week, which is
actually what reminded me to bring some gifts over. Hope you can join us
next time!

subject: content moderation at Riot
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I've been following Riot's expansion from text moderation into multilingual voice safety for VALORANT. 

 One challenge we see as teams scale across languages and modalities is keeping ground truth consistent: guidelines drift, edge cases multiply, and QA becomes increasingly difficult. 

 Curious if that's something your team is running into, or if the bigger challenge is improving model precision and reducing false positives?

subject: audit trail behind evicore's pa decisions
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I saw eviCore just went live with Pharmacy Forward last week and I know CMS's [YEAR] deadline for auditable, traceable authorization decisions is six months out. 

 We work with a top 3 US health-services firm running an internal LLM against clinical records for prior authorization. 

 The problem for them was building a layer where clinicians review the model's output against the source, flag what's wrong, and route the hard cases, with a full audit trail behind every decision.  

 With regulatory scrutiny on how medical criteria gets applied only growing, the audit trial is extremely important by [YEAR]! 

 I'd love to show you how we built it for them. Are you free Thursday or early next week?

subject: Cortex Launch with Seven Agents - One data problem
text:
Hi [NAME], 

Saw Cortex launch this week. Training a VLM on construction drawings while running document agents in parallel means two distinct data problems: labelled drawing sheets for the vision side, and output review to catch wrong answers before they reach a GC on a live project.

We worked with OnsiteIQ on their construction vision models. After moving their annotation and data infrastructure to Encord they hit 5x faster data throughput and cut project setup from 2 months to 2 weeks.

The pattern we see at teams your stage: the internal tooling that got you to launch stops scaling when model count and project volume rise at the same time. The slow part stops being generating outputs and starts being closing the loop between a model getting something wrong and a corrected example making it back into training.

Worth 20 minutes to talk through how you're handling that on the drawing side?

Please let me know.

subject: Data infrastructure behind [COMPANY]'s expansion
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I saw the tomosynthesis CE mark last month and the expansion into 10 European markets this year. 

 A significant acceleration with new modalities, new markets, new certification cycles, all on a team of ~50! 

 I've spent most of this year working with the Hoppr and Hologic engineering team on annotation and model validation infrastructure.  

 The specific friction points are usually the same: clinical annotators disengaging from tools that don't match their reading environment, QA overhead compounding per workload, and audit trail assembly becoming a manual burden at each certification cycle.

subject: Ankur Kapoor recommended we chat | Encord
text:
Hi [NAME],

Ankur suggested I reach out. For context, his team evaluated Encord
successfully last year, and having reconnected recently, he recommended
meeting with you, Sasha and Puneet as the next step.

He flagged three challenges Healthineers is facing:

   1. Stricter FDA/PCCP requirements on annotation and data residency
   2. Growing use of video training data, requiring multimodal annotation
   3. A fast-growing number of post-PoC models across types and disease
   areas

Encord addresses all three through unified curation and annotation, plus
external expert medical services.

We'd like to scope your team's needs and build a picture of how we can save
engineering time and improve model performance across all the Healthineers
teams.

We're on the East Coast late next week and the week after. When would work
to meet in-person?
